data.name: Fayha
data.gender_notes: Fayha is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is Joyful, Radiant, and Full of Happiness. The name Fayha carries the meaning “Joyful, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, English. Parents who choose Fayha usually hope their child will grow to embody joyful, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies the inner joy and happiness that comes from being close to Allah (God)
data.etymology: Fayha belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Joyful, Radiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fayha total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: فيهاء
in_arabic.meaning: اسم يدل على الخضرة والنماء والرخاء
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم علم مؤنث من أصل عربي، مشتق من فيهاء: الخضرة، النماء، الرخاء، والفيهاء: الأرض الخضراء، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة الأنعام: 'وَهَـذَا بَلَدٌ أَمِنٌ وَأَهلُهُ ثِقالُ أَيديهم في النَّدى وَجِراحَتي لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى فِي أَرضِهِ وَأَهليهِ وَخَيرَتي لَهُم في دُنيا الأَمانِ وَعَهدِ الأَمانِ وَأَرضٍ زُخرُفاً وَنَسيماً وَرَيحاناً'

in_english.name: Fayha
in_english.long_meaning: Fayha is an Arabic name that signifies lush greenery, growth, prosperity, and beauty. Etymologically derived from the Arabic root 'Fayh', it relates to concepts of fertility and abundance. Referenced in the Quran, specifically in Surah An'am, Fayha embodies spiritual and cultural significance in Islamic tradition, symbolizing a blessed and thriving existence

data.cultural_impact: The name Fayha is rooted in the Arabic language, which is the language of the Quran and the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). The name Fayha is derived from the Arabic root words "fa'ha" which means to be joyful, radiant, or full of happiness. In Islamic culture, the name Fayha reflects the positive and hopeful persona of the individual bearing it. The name can be considered a reminder to seek joy and happiness in life, as well as to spread it around as a means of uplifting the communities around us.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islam, the pursuit of happiness and joy is seen as a divine blessing from Allah. The Quran states "And Allah has willed to confer [this] favor on believers in estate and in their offspring and that they be enhanced in numbers, [and He has given them] a good word of praise from Him, and bountiful provision" [Quran 24:55]. The name Fayha serves as a reminder of this divine blessing and encourages the bearer to strive towards happiness and joy through good actions, strong faith, and a positive attitude, ultimately pleasing Allah and bringing spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Fayha signifies 'Delight' or 'Joy'. It is a reminder of the immense pleasure and bliss that comes with living a righteous and pious life according to the teachings of Islam. This joy is not transient but everlasting, as promised in the Quran, where true believers are described as those who will be in Paradise, "reclining on thrones, looking [in delight]" (Quran 36:56).

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Fayha was an important port city on the Red Sea coast, known for its thriving trade with Yemen and India during the Abbasid Caliphate (750-1258 AD). It was a major source of frankincense and myrrh, which were in high demand in the Mediterranean markets.
historical_references.context: Fayha was an important trading center during the Abbasid Caliphate, known for its production and export of frankincense and myrrh.

historical_references.reference: During the Ayyubid period (1171-1250 AD), Fayha became the capital of the Yemeni province, and was a center of Islamic scholarship and culture. Notable scholars such as Ibn al-Jawzi and Ibn al-Hajj al-Maliki lived and taught in Fayha during this time.
historical_references.context: Fayha was a center of Islamic scholarship and culture during the Ayyubid period.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Fayha, which means 'happy' or 'rejoicing' in Arabic, is increasingly seen as a symbol of joy, positivity, and empowerment in modern contexts. It is particularly popular among Arabic-speaking users on social media platforms such as Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok. On Instagram, Fayha is used as a hashtag (#Fayha) to tag posts about happiness, positivity, and self-expression. On YouTube, there are several channels and videos dedicated to Fayha, featuring music, dance, and comedy content that celebrates joy and happiness. On TikTok, Fayha is used as a challenge or trend, where users create and share videos showcasing their own happiness and joy. The trends of Arabic cultural revival, feminism and women's empowerment, and digital media and social networking are all contributing to the modern usage and popularity of the name Fayha.

name_in_real_life.story: Fatima Fayha, a teacher in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, shares that their name Fayha meaning "Joyful, Radiant" has been a source of inspiration throughout their life, motivating them to be a positive influence in their community.
